title: L2 Ricci Evidence-Bearing Session Artifact
description: Promotion-path contract for a single L2 order-book (depth-5) Ricci microstructure session. The README pins L2 Ricci at HYPOTHESIS-tier and explicitly forbids promotion until a real depth-5 session with a real data hash, replay, baseline, null model, falsifier, and negative evidence is recorded. This schema is the machine-checkable counterpart of docs/research/l2_ricci_evidence_protocol.md: every field it requires is a precondition for any L2 Ricci claim to move beyond HYPOTHESIS. It is line-specific (depth_level is pinned to 5) and complements the line-agnostic research_inference_artifact envelope; it does not replace it. Anchored on W3C PROV-DM (provenance), RO-Crate 1.1 (conformsTo), SLSA Provenance v1 (builder/inputs), and the pre-registration discipline used by ricci_microstructure_v1.

conforms_to.description: RO-Crate 1.1 conformsTo: the resolvable $id of the schema this session artifact pledges to. Optional, but when present must match this schema's $id so a machine can fetch the exact contract it was validated against.

git_sha.description: 40-hex git commit the session was produced at. PROV-DM wasGeneratedBy; pins the code that computed the session.

data_sha256.description: sha256 over the canonical L2 depth-5 order-book session capture. A zero hash is schema-valid but is a HYPOTHESIS-tier placeholder; the semantic-truth gate (semantic_validation_status) bars a zero hash from claiming evidence. There is no real depth-5 Ricci result until this hashes real captured data.

config_sha256.description: sha256 over the pinned run configuration (window, metric, null specification, cost model) that the session was computed under.

venue.description: Lowercase venue/exchange identifier the depth-5 book was captured from (e.g. 'binance', 'cme').

symbol.description: Instrument symbol for the captured book (e.g. 'BTCUSDT').

depth_level.description: L2 order-book depth. Pinned to 5: this contract is exclusively for the depth-5 microstructure session that the README names as the gate to leave HYPOTHESIS. Any other depth is a different (uncontracted) experiment and is rejected.

session_start_utc.description: UTC start of the capture session (RFC 3339, trailing 'Z').

session_end_utc.description: UTC end of the capture session (RFC 3339, trailing 'Z'). Must be at or after session_start_utc; that ordering is enforced by the validator (a schema alone cannot compare two field values).

baseline_id.description: Identifier of the reference baseline the session score is judged against. A result with no baseline is asserted, not falsified; required for promotion.

null_model_id.description: Identifier of the registered null model (e.g. 'permutation_null') the session is tested against. Required for promotion: a signal that does not beat a null is not evidence.

falsifier_id.description: Identifier of the executable falsifier that could have killed the hypothesis. Required for promotion: an unfalsifiable claim cannot be promoted.

replay_command.description: Exact shell command that recomputes this session from committed inputs (data_sha256, config_sha256, git_sha). Claims recomputation, not cross-environment bit-equality (the repo's CALIB-GRID F3 result shows cross-BLAS bit-identity is not guaranteed). For an evidence session the command must be executable (begin with 'python ' or 'python3 '); for a placeholder/pending session it must be honestly marked as not-yet-runnable by setting replay_blocked: true. A silently-non-runnable command (neither executable nor blocked) is rejected by the validator. Required for promotion: a result that cannot be replayed is not evidence.

replay_blocked.description: Honest flag that the replay_command cannot yet be run (e.g. no real depth-5 capture exists, so the recompute would have nothing to recompute). When true, the session is barred from any evidence status: a blocked replay is not a replay. When absent or false, the validator requires replay_command to be an executable 'python'/'python3' invocation. Default false.

claim.description: The specific sub-claim the falsification attempt targeted (e.g. 'depth-5 Ricci IC survives a permutation null').

outcome.description: Result of the attempt. SURVIVED = the claim was not killed by this attack (information). KILLED = the claim was falsified. BLOCKED = the attempt could not run (e.g. placeholder data).

detail.description: What was attempted and what was observed, in enough detail to reproduce the reasoning.

negative_evidence.description: Recorded falsification attempts (survival paths and kills), not victories. A session with zero negative-evidence entries has not been adversarially tested and cannot be promoted. At least one entry is required by schema; the validator additionally requires that no required falsification axis is silently omitted.

semantic_validation_status.description: Honest self-label of the session's evidentiary state. PLACEHOLDER = schema-shaped skeleton with no real data (zero hashes); never evidence. PENDING = real inputs declared, falsification not yet adjudicated. PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED = the semantic-truth + falsification battery ran with that verdict. Only PASS, with real (non-zero) hashes and complete provenance, authorises promotion beyond HYPOTHESIS.
